quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04024_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྒྱུད་བླ་མ། (Ratnagotravibhāga, Tengyur D4024) ལེའུ་དང་པོ། དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་གྱི་སྐབས། ཀུན་རྫོབ་དང་དོན་དམ་པའི་སྐྱབས།
quotes.why: Maitreya's root verse: its first three lines are p397's proof text, its fourth line is the one this paragraph quotes twice — cited here from the Tengyur, where it belongs.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04025_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS RNAM PAR BSHAD PA (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་རྣམ་བཤད། (Asaṅga's Vyākhyā, Tengyur D4025) on the same verse.
quotes.why: Asaṅga's gloss of the fourth line — the assembly of the three vehicles reaches its end by attaining the fully pure dharmakāya — which is what the yig cha's སངས་རྒྱས་ཐོབ་པ་ན་སྐྱབས་དེའི་མཐར་ཐུག་པར་འགྱུར་བ paraphrases.

Tsongkhapa raising the very qualm the paragraph opens with and answering it — the source behind the yig cha's གསེར་ཕྲེང་ལས citation, though in different words, and naming the Dharma Jewel as well as the Saṅgha.

Chökyi Gyaltsen earlier in this same excursus committing himself to the Buddha-ārya being the Saṅgha Jewel, on pain of there being no ultimate Three Jewels — the premise this paragraph's answer silently relies on.

Haribhadra's gloss on the instruction concerning the Saṅgha: the Saṅgha to be instructed excludes the arhat who is 'included within the Buddha Jewel' — the one point where the Indian commentary touches this paragraph's question.
The root-verse lines on the ten instructions; the whole refuge excursus in the yig cha hangs from the second of them.

Chökyi Gyaltsen's own statement of the objection — a composite of a Buddha and a path-of-seeing bodhisattva — that the qualifier ཁྱོད་ཡིན་པའམ་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ནང་ཚན་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་དོན་དམ་པའི་སྐྱབས་མེད་པ exists to block.
The mtha' dpyod's alternative ('or else') wording of both definitions — qualified symmetrically, where the spyi don qualifies only the conventional refuge.

Gyaltsab Je's account of the two refuges, the source of the phrase དངོས་པོའི་གནས་ཚོད་ལ་ལམ་གྱི་བགྲོད་པ་མཐར་ཐུག་མ་ཐུག — paired in his version with a clause about how the seeker holds it (བསམ་ངོར) that the yig cha drops.

quotes.file: Sungbum/SEMS TZAM_MIND-ONLY SCHOOL (CHITTAMATRA)/RGYUD BLA MA (UTTARATANTRA)_THE HIGHER LINE/S05434M_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I t'IKKA_@_RGYAL TSAB DAR MA RIN CHEN (1364-1432)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je's word-commentary on the Uttaratantra reading the fourth line as a reason why the Buddha alone is the ultimate refuge — the assembly of āryas up to the end of the tenth ground has the dharmakāya as its end.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/MKHAS GRUB BSTAN PA DAR RGYAS_KEDRUP TENPA DARGYE (1493-1568)/SPYI DON_OVERVIEW/SE00009M1_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN RTZA 'GREL GYI SPYI DON RNAM BSHAD SNYING PO RGYAN GYI SNANG BA, CHA DANG PO_'An Illumination of the 'Jewel of the Essence of Good Explanation',' being an Overview of the Root Text and Commentary_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The Sera Mey yig cha answering the identical qualm with three reasons — dharmakāya, the Dharma Jewel as the cessation and path in the Buddha's continuum, and the learners culminating there — where Chökyi Gyaltsen gives only the Saṅgha.
A distant text that names which part of the Buddha is the ultimate Saṅgha — the two form bodies — a specification Chökyi Gyaltsen does not make.
A dissenting voice: the text rejects as confused both the view that nothing satisfying the definitions of the latter two Jewels is an ultimate refuge and the view that the form bodies are.
Gyaltsab Je: the ultimate refuge is the Buddha as having the nature of the three bodies — form bodies included, against the position the Rol mtsho takes.
Jamyang Zhepa's Gomang definition of the ultimate refuge, framed by how the goal appears as well as by how it really is — close to Gyaltsab's two-sided gloss, unlike the yig cha's single criterion.
